title: A Log That Cannot Fill the Disk: Rotation Under a Byte Budget, and a Guard Against One Error Said a Million Times

questions.question: Why is a full disk worse than a program that cannot write its log?
options: A full disk makes the robot reboot
It stops everything else that writes: the configuration, the black box dump, the next update, temporary files
A full disk deletes the oldest log by itself
It is not worse: only logging stops
questions.explanation: Everything that writes shares the disk. When it is full the configuration cannot be saved, the black box cannot be dumped and the next update cannot be stored.

questions.question: With 10 MB files, 20 files and 200 MB, how much can the log take in the steady state?
options: 2 GB: files times the total
10 MB, one file
As much as the disk holds
200 MB: the smaller of the total and files times file size
questions.explanation: The budget is whichever limit is tighter. Twenty files of 10 MB is exactly 200 MB; with at most 5 files it would be 50 MB.

questions.question: A day at 100 KB/s fills a 4 GB disk after how long with no limit?
options: 24 hours, exactly a day
11.1 hours: the robot dies in its first shift
1 hour
Never: 100 KB/s is too slow to matter
questions.explanation: 100 KB a second is 8.6 GB a day. A 4 GB disk is full in 11.1 hours; with the budget the same day peaked at 199 MB.

questions.question: Why is the current file never deleted?
options: Deleting it would lose the record just written: a record bigger than the whole budget is kept until the next one arrives
The current file is locked by the operating system
It is always empty when rotation runs
Deleting it would break the file numbering
questions.explanation: A record larger than the whole budget is usually the one somebody wanted, a stack trace or a dump. It is kept until the next record closes its file.

questions.question: A camera says the same error 1000 times a second for 10 s. How many are written and how many counted?
options: 10000 written and none suppressed
1 written, 9999 suppressed
5 written, 9995 suppressed and counted, handed over once as a summary
None written, 10000 counted
questions.explanation: The first five in a window of 10 s are written and the rest are counted, to be reported once as a single line. A different message is not held back.

questions.question: Why does rotation without a guard still lose?
options: The repeated message fills the budget and pushes out the history that explains it, deleted by the fault itself
Rotation deletes the newest file first
Rotation cannot run while a message repeats
It does not lose anything: the budget protects the history
questions.explanation: A flood of one line fills every file in the budget. The half hour before the fault, which would explain it, is what gets deleted.
